places.note: Main's corrected per-place product (each place's own sky, lightning and haze).

evidence: A literature inventory of lunar lava-tube candidates set against the 28% atlas (LOLA 16 px/deg less the degree-200 geoid); a two-dimensional Dupuit groundwater solve on the atlas about each land candidate, checked against the analytic mound; closed-form seepage, conduction and view-factor physics at lunar gravity with Earth basalt and tunnelling values carried over; and grid sums of the atlas, the design climatology and the lightning map over the highlands, with the engineering lattice model sized for building towers. Tube sizes rest on remote sensing (pit imaging, rille morphology, gravity and radar) and are bounds and estimates; no tube interior beyond tens of metres from a pit has been seen. The groundwater solve takes uniform rock over a flat base at the atlas's 7.6 km cells; nothing here is a structural or radiation-transport model.
reading_rule: Heights in m or km above the 28% sea level unless named; longitudes east. Areas km2, people in millions or billions as named, power MW or GW as named, water km3 a year. Ranges are [low, high] or low/central/high cases as labelled. Water tables are the atlas cell's steady level from the two-dimensional solve, capped by the cell's mean ground, set against the candidate's own ground; heads are metres of water at lunar gravity, with the Earth head that gives the same pressure beside them.

water_table.rule: low: least recharge, most permeable and thickest basalt; high: the reverse
water_table.base: a flat base the basalt thickness below the window's lowest water; Gong et al. measure the thickness down from the mare surface, so under high ground the basalt may end above that base and the saturated column then runs into the crust below
water_table.rise_start: the water table at the sea's level under the land when the rain begins

capacity.section: a semi-elliptical vault over a flat floor; a level counts where a full storey of headroom remains

grail_section.basis: the lowest ten levels in a semi-elliptical vault

airless_deep.basis: a constant -20 C inside tubes (Hörz 1985, after Mendell); 253 K

near_skylight.basis: beyond the opening in permanent shadow, about 290 K and nearly constant, as a blackbody cavity at 1 AU (Horvath et al. 2022)

interiors_from_albedo.basis: thermal equilibrium from the holes' albedo (Haruyama et al. 2010)

effective_dose_by_depth_msv_year.basis: GCR at solar minimum under 5 m of the airless surface's loose layer over 3.3 g/cm3 basalt; read from De Angelis et al. 2002, Fig. 3; none observable past 6 m

shallow_per_year.basis: 28 shallow (high-frequency teleseismic) moonquakes in 1971-1976 on the Apollo network, "averaging about five per year"

largest_mb.basis: the largest in eight years of observation

site_mb_4_5_within_100_km.basis: a lunar base at a random site

largest_observed_mb.basis: the largest shallow moonquake observed, on a b-value of 0.55; extrapolated, magnitude 7-7.5 somewhere on the Moon once in 50-100 years

near_scarps.basis: epicentres within the distance of strong shaking from young thrust-fault scarps

quakes.analogue: a rate like the central United States' intraplate seismicity, where rare large events (New Madrid, mb 7.1-7.4) cannot be ruled out (Oberst & Nakamura 1992)

ways_of_living_home.note: the highland towns' and terrain-held districts' shared home: the ground 4 km up left once the metropolis circle, the shores of seas and great lakes and the wet margins have taken theirs

comfort.definition: comfortable: air at 2 m of 18-26 C with a dewpoint of at most 15 C (strict), or 17-27 C and 16 C (loose), as the climate products define it
